model.name: Concept / Term
model.purpose: Represent a stable semantic concept that is independent of any single label, and govern how that concept is placed in concept schemes, related to other concepts inside a scheme, mapped to concepts in other schemes, aligned to formal ontology terms, and exchanged across systems and serializations.
model.scope_statement: This is the relationship, scheme and interoperability portion of WM-KNW-006. The concept is the aggregate root: terms, labels, mappings and grouping nodes describe or reference it but never replace its identity. In scope: concept-scheme membership and top concepts; grouping constructs (collections, arrays, concept groups, classification levels); within-scheme hierarchical and associative relations including their refined kinds; compound-concept modelling and decomposition cautions; cross-scheme mapping relations, mapping sets and chain limits; multilingual and cross-lingual mapping caveats; semantic alignment to ontology classes and properties; and import, export, projection and crosswalk behaviour. The model is storage-format and interface neutral: RDF, JSON, YAML, Markdown, tabular files, Git, MCP and document stores are projections of the same assertion set, not its semantics. Core lexical and definition content, lifecycle and versioning, governance and authority, provenance, access decisions and quality measurement are handled by other areas of the same model or by referenced models, and appear here only as boundaries and binding references.
in_scope: Assertions that a concept is in, or is a top concept of, one or more concept schemes, including the zero-scheme and multi-scheme cases
Membership in non-hierarchical grouping constructs: collections, ordered collections, thesaurus arrays, concept groups and micro-thesauri, and declared classification levels
Direct within-scheme hierarchical relations and the explicit separation of asserted direct links from derived transitive closure
Refined hierarchical kinds (generic, partitive, instantial) and refined associative kinds where the governing scheme supports them
Associative relations, their symmetry, and their declared disjointness from the hierarchical closure
Compound (pre-coordinated) concepts, the decision to pre- or post-coordinate, and the limits of lexical decomposition as evidence of semantic composition
Cross-scheme mapping relation types, their formal properties (symmetry, transitivity, disjointness) and their binding to specific scheme releases
Mapping sets and correspondences, including reified many-to-many associations, cardinality and conservative chain-composition rules
Cross-lingual equivalence degrees and BCP 47 language, script and region scoping of multilingual assertions
Semantic alignment predicates pointing at ontology classes, properties and individuals, with the entailment each predicate commits a consumer to
Import, export, projection and crosswalk behaviour: closure selection, dangling-reference handling, lossy-construct declaration and namespace resolution
out_of_scope: Preferred, alternative and hidden label structure, literal forms, definitions, scope notes, editorial notes and other lexical or documentary content of the concept
Lifecycle states, versioning, deprecation and succession of concepts, terms and schemes, including issuance of scheme releases referenced here only as binding parameters
Governance, maintenance-agency authority, approval workflow, change proposal and dispute resolution
Provenance records, contributor attribution and evidence packages beyond the reference a relation needs to be interpretable
Access-control decisions, permission evaluation and enforcement gating
Retention scheduling, physical erasure and legal disposition of records
Quality measurement frameworks, scoring models and vocabulary-level fitness assessment
OWL entailment execution, reasoner configuration, closure materialisation scheduling and inference-engine operation
Automatic mapping generation, similarity scoring algorithms and machine-learning alignment pipelines
Catalogue and dataset description records that reference a scheme as a theme taxonomy
Retrieval, indexing and query-expansion behaviour of downstream search systems

boundary_notes.neighbor: Term, label and lexical structure of WM-KNW-006
boundary_notes.distinction: The concept is identified independently of any label. SKOS-XL reifies labels and permits label-to-label relations, and OntoLex-Lemon models lexical entries, forms and senses; both are referenced here only when a relation or mapping must be scoped by a label or language. Literal forms, preferred-term selection and label relations are owned by the lexical area.

The scheme as a managed object - its maintenance agency, coverage statement, release policy and publication - is owned by the parent. This area carries only the concept's membership assertion, top-concept declaration, and the scheme reference needed to bind a mapping.

iso-thes status values and scheme release identifiers are carried here as binding parameters of a relation or mapping set. State transitions, succession of superseded concepts and release issuance are not modelled or executed here.

This model records which relations are asserted and which are derived, and declares which entailment an alignment predicate commits a consumer to. It does not own OWL entailment, reasoner configuration, materialisation scheduling or query-time inference execution.

SKOS integrity conditions are checked here as alignments and reported as findings. Enforcement gating, approval of exceptions, persistence of audit trails and access decisions are executed by the governance area or the adopting Dimension.

A scheme may be referenced by a catalogue as a theme taxonomy and a concept used as a theme. Catalogue records, distributions and dataset series are outside this model; only the fact that a concept is referenceable by IRI matters here.

Transitive closure, mapping chains and collection membership are supplied as navigable structure with explicit composition limits. How a search engine expands a query, weights a broader term or ranks results is a consumer concern.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Normative source for skos:ConceptScheme, inScheme, hasTopConcept/topConceptOf, semanticRelation, broader/narrower and their non-transitivity, broaderTransitive/narrowerTransitive, related, Collection/OrderedCollection/member/memberList, mappingRelation and the match properties, plus integrity conditions S5-S9, S27, S36, S37 and S46 and the statement that mapping properties are only used across schemes by convention.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Primer
sources.relevance: Non-normative but first-party guidance on top concepts as entry points, the semantic-versus-mapping distinction, pre- and post-coordination and the absence of an established SKOS pre-coordination pattern, collections as non-concept grouping, multilingual labelling limits, and the explicit statement that closeMatch is not transitive while exactMatch is.

sources.title: SKOS eXtension for Labels (SKOS-XL) namespace document
sources.relevance: Defines skosxl:Label, literalForm, prefLabel/altLabel/hiddenLabel and the symmetric skosxl:labelRelation, used here only to mark the boundary between concept-level relations and label-level relations.

sources.title: ISO 25964 - the international standard for thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies
sources.version_or_date: ISO 25964-1:2011 and ISO 25964-2:2013; NISO-maintained standard information page
sources.relevance: Authoritative description of the ISO 25964 data model (concepts, terms, concept groups, arrays, relationships) and of Part 2 mapping categories: equivalence (exact, inexact, partial), hierarchical and associative mappings, plus compound equivalence for one-to-many mapping of pre-coordinated concepts, and the published SKOS/SKOS-XL correspondence.

sources.title: ISO 25964 SKOS extension (iso-thes) namespace document
sources.organization: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (hosting the ISO 25964 working-group namespace)
sources.relevance: Machine-readable constructs used for refined structure: ThesaurusArray with superOrdinate/subordinateArray, ConceptGroup with microThesaurusOf, broaderGeneric/broaderPartitive/broaderInstantial, CompoundEquivalence with plusUF/plusUse, SplitNonPreferredTerm, PreferredTerm and status.

sources.title: XKOS: An SKOS extension for representing statistical classifications
sources.relevance: Defines ClassificationLevel, levels, depth and numberOfLevels; Correspondence, ConceptAssociation, compares, sourceConcept and targetConcept for many-to-many cross-scheme and cross-version mapping; and refined relations specializes/generalizes, isPartOf/hasPart, causal, sequential (precedes/succeeds transitive, previous/next non-transitive) and temporal before/after.

sources.title: Lexicon Model for Ontologies: Community Report (OntoLex-lemon)
sources.relevance: Defines LexicalEntry, Form, LexicalSense and LexicalConcept (a subclass of skos:Concept), the denotes/reference/evokes/lexicalizedSense bridge to ontology terms, the vartrans module for translation and lexico-semantic relations, and the decomp module (subterm, constituent, Component, correspondsTo) whose decomposition is lexical rather than semantic. Explicitly not a W3C Standard.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Establishes the entailment consequences of owl:equivalentClass, rdfs:subClassOf (transitive and reflexive), owl:sameAs and owl:disjointWith, and the distinction between class equivalence and individual identity - the basis for treating an alignment predicate as a commitment rather than a label.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax
sources.relevance: Grounds format neutrality: the abstract syntax of IRIs, literals, language-tagged strings, triples, graphs and datasets is independent of concrete serialization, and IRIs have global scope so two appearances denote the same resource.

sources.title: Tags for Identifying Languages (BCP 47 / RFC 5646)
sources.relevance: Defines language, extended-language, script, region, variant, extension and private-use subtags, canonical case conventions and matching caveats. A tag identifies the language of content and does not by itself assert semantic equivalence between two tagged strings.

sources.title: Best Practice Recipes for Publishing RDF Vocabularies
sources.relevance: Guidance on hash versus slash namespace design, dereferenceable term identifiers, content negotiation and keeping term identifiers stable while version information moves into the served document - the basis for namespace and identifier-resolution rules in interchange.

sources.title: ANSI/NISO Z39.19-2005 (R2010) Guidelines for the Construction, Format, and Management of Monolingual Controlled Vocabularies
sources.relevance: US national standard for the contents, display, construction, testing, maintenance and management of monolingual controlled vocabularies (lists, synonym rings, taxonomies, thesauri); cited as an independent authority that controlled-vocabulary relationship structure is standardised practice, not local convention. The full normative text is behind a download and its clause-level rules were not verified here.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Defines dcat:themeTaxonomy as a knowledge organization system used to classify catalogued resources and dcat:theme as a category, and recommends that such taxonomies be organised as a skos:ConceptScheme, skos:Collection, owl:Ontology or similar so each member is denoted by an IRI - evidence for external consumption of schemes and for the catalogue boundary.

sources.title: ISO 1087:2019 Terminology work and terminology science - Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Terminology-science vocabulary distinguishing object, concept and designation, and defining intension, extension, characteristics and hierarchical relation types (generic and partitive). Cited only as corroboration for the generic/partitive distinction; the ISO catalogue page blocks automated retrieval, so no clause text was read and no claim rests on this source alone.

bundles.name: Scheme placement and grouping
bundles.description: Where a concept sits: which concept schemes assert it, whether it is a declared entry point into a hierarchy, and which non-hierarchical grouping constructs (collections, arrays, concept groups, classification levels) contain it.
bundles.rationale: SKOS treats scheme membership as an assertion about curation context rather than about meaning: a concept may be in zero, one or many schemes, membership does not propagate along semantic relations, and grouping constructs are formally disjoint from concepts. An agent that conflates placement with meaning will over-infer, so placement is separated from relation semantics at the top level.

layers.name: Concept-scheme membership and entry points
layers.description: Assertions binding a concept to concept schemes and declaring it a top concept, together with the rules governing multi-scheme participation, non-propagation of membership and hierarchy entry.

findings.name: Concept-scheme membership and multi-scheme participation
findings.description: SKOS places no cardinality constraint on membership: there are no conditions preventing a concept from taking part in zero, one or more than one concept scheme, skos:inScheme is not declared transitive, and a semantic link between two concepts does not entail that both are in the same scheme. Membership must therefore be asserted per concept per scheme, and an implementation that derives it from relations is making a local rule, not a standard entailment. skos:topConceptOf is a sub-property of skos:inScheme, so a top-concept declaration also asserts membership.

questions.text: Which concept schemes does this concept assert membership in, and is one of them designated the maintenance scheme that issues its authoritative identifier?
answer_data: Scheme reference (identifier or IRI) for each asserted membership
Flag or reference marking the maintenance scheme, where one is designated
Note recording that the zero-scheme and multi-scheme cases are both permitted by the standard

questions.text: Does this deployment permit a concept to belong to more than one scheme, and what local rule resolves conflicting structure between those schemes?

Reference to the governing scheme whose rules were applied

data_elements.name: Concept scheme membership reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a concept scheme in which this concept is asserted to be a member.

data_elements.name: Maintenance scheme reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the scheme whose maintenance agency issues the concept's authoritative identifier, where one is designated.

data_elements.name: Membership assertion mode
data_elements.description: Coded value distinguishing an explicitly asserted membership from one derived by a local rule, since the standard supplies no derivation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Membership is a set of assertions linking two identifiers plus a small number of coded qualifiers. It has no document body, no rendition and no content to fix by digest; producing a separate artifact would create a second place where the same reference could drift out of step with the concept record.

findings.name: Top concepts and hierarchy entry points
findings.description: skos:hasTopConcept has domain skos:ConceptScheme and range skos:Concept, and skos:topConceptOf is its inverse and a sub-property of skos:inScheme. Critically, the SKOS Reference defines no integrity condition preventing a declared top concept from also asserting a broader concept in the same scheme. A top concept is therefore a declared entry point chosen by the scheme, not a root derived from the absence of a broader link; treating it as a derived root is a common but unsupported assumption.

questions.text: Which schemes declare this concept a top concept, and is that declaration made by the scheme rather than inferred from missing broader links?
answer_data: Reference to each scheme declaring this concept a top concept
Source of the declaration: scheme assertion or local inference
Note that topConceptOf also entails scheme membership

questions.text: Does a concept declared as a top concept also assert a broader concept within the same scheme, and how is that reconciled?
answer_data: Boolean flag recording coexistence of a top-concept declaration and an in-scheme broader link
Local reconciliation rule, with the note that SKOS supplies no integrity condition here
List of affected concept and scheme pairs

answer_data: Entry-point rule, for example concepts with no asserted broader link in the scheme
Deterministic ordering rule for presenting entry points
Statement that a computed entry set is derived and not written back as a declaration

answer_data: Per-scheme record of the concept's structural position

Validation output flagging cross-scheme position mismatches

data_elements.description: Reference to each scheme that declares this concept one of its top concepts.

data_elements.name: Hierarchy entry-point rule

findings.inline_only_rationale: Top-concept declarations are directed assertions between a scheme identifier and a concept identifier, plus one consistency flag. There is no renderable body and no interchange payload distinct from the scheme export already covered by the interchange finding, so a separate artifact would duplicate state.

layers.name: Grouping, array and level constructs
layers.description: Non-hierarchical grouping of concepts: SKOS collections and ordered collections, ISO 25964 thesaurus arrays and concept groups, and XKOS classification levels, all of which are formally distinct from concepts and must not be exported as retrievable concepts.

findings.name: Collections, arrays, concept groups and classification levels
findings.description: skos:Collection and skos:OrderedCollection group concepts through skos:member and the functional skos:memberList, with every list item also a member (S36); collections are disjoint from both skos:Concept and skos:ConceptScheme (S37). ISO 25964 adds ThesaurusArray with superOrdinate and subordinateArray for sibling grouping under a node label or facet indicator, and ConceptGroup with microThesaurusOf for domain subsets. XKOS adds ClassificationLevel with levels, depth and numberOfLevels. Because grouping nodes are not concepts, a hierarchical link between a parent concept and its children must still be asserted concept to concept; relying on the array to carry the hierarchy silently breaks navigation.

questions.text: Which collections, thesaurus arrays or concept groups include this concept, and is any of those memberships ordered?
answer_data: Reference to each grouping construct containing the concept
Construct type: collection, ordered collection, thesaurus array or concept group
Position within an ordered member list where ordering applies

answer_data: Type discriminator distinguishing grouping nodes from concepts

List of identifiers typed as both, if any

findings.inline_only_rationale: Grouping membership, array superordinates and level depth are reference and scalar values attached to the concept and to the grouping node. Ordered collections are carried as a position value rather than a stored list document, so there is no independent content object to identify, version or verify by digest.

bundles.name: Within-scheme semantic relations
bundles.description: Relations asserted between concepts inside one concept scheme: direct hierarchical links and their derived transitive closure, refined hierarchical kinds, associative relations and their disjointness from hierarchy, and the modelling of compound (pre-coordinated) concepts.
bundles.rationale: SKOS deliberately does not declare skos:broader or skos:narrower transitive and asserts them only for direct links, while providing separate transitive properties and declaring skos:related disjoint from the transitive hierarchical closure. These are the constraints most often violated by implementations, so asserted structure, derived structure and refined typing are separated and treated conservatively.

layers.name: Hierarchical and associative relations
layers.description: The direct relation assertions a concept makes inside its scheme, the refinement of hierarchical kind, the associative relation, and the transitivity, symmetry and disjointness rules that constrain all of them.

findings.name: Direct hierarchical assertion versus derived transitive closure
findings.description: skos:broader and skos:narrower are inverses and are, by convention, used only to assert direct hierarchical links; neither is declared transitive. skos:broaderTransitive and skos:narrowerTransitive are the transitive properties that capture direct or indirect links. The operational consequence is that ancestor and descendant sets are derived views: they may be computed at query time or materialised for performance, but must never be written back as if they were asserted direct links, because that destroys the ability to reconstruct the authored hierarchy.

questions.text: Which broader and narrower concepts does this concept assert, and is every one of them a direct link rather than an ancestor or descendant?
answer_data: Reference to each directly asserted broader concept
Reference to each directly asserted narrower concept
Assertion marker distinguishing authored direct links from computed ones

questions.text: Is the transitive form of the hierarchy computed at read time, materialised in storage, or both, and how is materialised closure marked as derived?
answer_data: Closure materialisation mode
Marker applied to every derived transitive statement
Recomputation trigger when a direct link changes

questions.text: Does this concept assert more than one broader concept, and does the governing scheme permit polyhierarchy?

Reference to the scheme whose rule was applied

List of concept identifiers participating in any cycle
Rejection or quarantine rule applied to a cyclic assertion

answer_data: Local rule permitting or forbidding cross-scheme hierarchical links
Discriminator recording whether the link is a semantic relation or a mapping relation
Note that SKOS permits semantic relations across schemes but that mapping properties are the conventional construct

data_elements.name: Direct broader concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a concept asserted as a direct broader concept; ancestors reachable only transitively are excluded.

data_elements.name: Direct narrower concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a concept asserted as a direct narrower concept; descendants reachable only transitively are excluded.

data_elements.name: Transitive closure materialisation mode
data_elements.description: Coded value stating whether transitive hierarchy is computed on demand, materialised and marked derived, or not provided.

data_elements.name: Polyhierarchy permission flag
data_elements.description: Boolean recording whether the governing scheme permits a concept to assert more than one broader concept.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Hierarchical structure is a set of directed references between concept identifiers plus derivation flags. The derived closure is intentionally not persisted as an addressable object, so there is nothing here with independent content, rendition or integrity requirements to justify an artifact.

findings.name: Hierarchical relation kinds: generic, partitive and instantial
findings.description: SKOS offers a single undifferentiated broader relation. ISO 25964, through iso-thes, refines it into broaderGeneric, broaderPartitive and broaderInstantial, and XKOS distinguishes specializes/generalizes from isPartOf/hasPart. ISO 1087 gives the corresponding terminology-science distinction between generic and partitive relations. The refinement matters operationally because chaining behaves differently: generic subsumption composes reliably, whereas partitive chains are unsafe across changes of part-whole kind. Projecting a refined kind onto plain broader for interchange is lossy and must be declared.

questions.text: What kind of hierarchical relation is asserted to each broader concept - generic, partitive, instantial or undifferentiated?
answer_data: Coded relation kind per broader assertion
Vocabulary the kind is drawn from, such as the ISO 25964 or XKOS refinement set
Default kind applied when the scheme does not refine

questions.text: Which test must be satisfied before a hierarchical relation is asserted, and is the justification recorded with the assertion?
answer_data: Named test applied, such as the all-and-some subsumption test for generic relations
Short justification note attached to the assertion
Rule stating whether an untested assertion may be created at all

questions.text: Which hierarchical kinds may be chained transitively in this deployment, and at which point must a chain stop?
answer_data: Per-kind chaining rule
Stop condition where the kind changes along a path
Statement that SKOS itself declares transitivity only for broaderTransitive, not for the refined kinds

questions.text: What information is lost when a refined hierarchical kind is projected onto plain broader or narrower for interchange?
answer_data: List of refined kinds collapsed in the projection
Declaration that the projection is lossy and not reversible from the output alone
Retention of the refined kind in the source record

data_elements.name: Hierarchical relation kind
data_elements.description: Coded refinement of a hierarchical assertion: generic, partitive, instantial or undifferentiated.

data_elements.name: Hierarchical assertion justification
data_elements.description: Short note recording which test justified the hierarchical assertion, held with the relation rather than as a separate evidence record.

data_elements.name: Hierarchical chaining rule
data_elements.description: Coded rule stating whether and how far assertions of this kind may be composed into a transitive path.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Relation kind, justification note and chaining rule are qualifiers on an existing relation assertion. They have no standalone existence: detaching them into an artifact would separate a qualifier from the assertion it qualifies and create an orphaning risk with no compensating benefit.

findings.name: Associative relations and disjointness from hierarchy
findings.description: skos:related is symmetric and is not transitive, and integrity condition S27 declares it disjoint with skos:broaderTransitive - so two concepts connected by any hierarchical path must not also be linked associatively. XKOS refines association into causal (causes, causedBy), sequential (precedes and succeeds, which are transitive, versus previous and next, which are not) and temporal (before, after). Because symmetry is a property of the relation rather than of the record, a deployment must decide once whether the inverse statement is stored or inferred, and apply that decision uniformly.

questions.text: Which associative relations does this concept assert, and is a refined association subtype recorded for each?
answer_data: Reference to each associatively related concept
Coded association subtype where refinement is used, such as causal, sequential or temporal
Scheme context in which the association was asserted

questions.text: How is the rule that an associative link must not coexist with a hierarchical path between the same two concepts checked?
answer_data: Validation result over the transitive hierarchical closure for each associative pair
List of pairs violating the disjointness condition
Resolution rule choosing which assertion is withdrawn

questions.text: Is the inverse of each associative assertion stored explicitly, inferred at read time, or both?
answer_data: Inverse storage mode applied uniformly across the deployment
Rule preventing double counting when both directions are stored
Behaviour on export when only one direction is present in the source

questions.text: Which refined associative relations may be composed transitively and which are explicitly non-transitive?
answer_data: Per-subtype transitivity declaration
Explicit statement that the base associative relation is not transitive

data_elements.name: Associatively related concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a concept linked by an associative relation.

data_elements.name: Association subtype
data_elements.description: Coded refinement of an associative relation, such as causal, sequential or temporal, drawn from an extension vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Inverse assertion storage mode
data_elements.description: Coded decision on whether the symmetric counterpart of an associative assertion is stored, inferred or both.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Associative structure consists of symmetric references and coded subtypes attached to the concept. The disjointness check produces a transient report consumed by the validation area rather than a record this model owns, so no artifact is declared here.

layers.name: Compound concepts and decomposition
layers.description: Whether a concept is pre-coordinated, how its components are recorded without over-claiming, and how one-to-many compound equivalence is expressed when a concept can only be matched by combining several concepts in another vocabulary.

findings.name: Compound concepts, coordination choice and decomposition cautions
findings.description: A knowledge organization system may pre-coordinate a compound concept as a single unit or leave the combination to retrieval time (post-coordination). The SKOS Primer records that established patterns for pre-coordination have not emerged in the SKOS community and recommends extensions rather than additions to the core vocabulary, so a deployment must state its own rule. OntoLex decomp offers subterm, constituent and Component, but this decomposes a lexical entry, not a concept: a recorded lexical decomposition must never be read as a claim that the concept is the semantic composition of its parts.

questions.text: Is this concept a pre-coordinated compound, and which concepts are recorded as its components?
answer_data: Coordination mode: pre-coordinated compound or atomic
Reference to each recorded component concept
Scheme rule that permitted the compound to be created

questions.text: Under which rule was this combination modelled as one concept rather than left to be combined at retrieval time?
answer_data: Named coordination rule applied by the scheme
Reason the combination is treated as a stable unit of meaning
Note recording that no standard SKOS pre-coordination pattern is available

questions.text: Is the recorded decomposition lexical or semantic, and what must a consumer not infer from it?
answer_data: Decomposition basis: lexical form decomposition or asserted semantic composition
Explicit non-inference statement covering hierarchy and equivalence
Reference to the lexical model where form-level decomposition is owned

answer_data: Relation construct used to link compound to component
Statement that the link is not asserted as broader, narrower or a match

data_elements.name: Coordination mode
data_elements.description: Coded value recording whether the concept is a pre-coordinated compound or an atomic concept intended for post-coordination.

data_elements.name: Component concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a concept recorded as a component of this compound concept, without any implied hierarchical or equivalence claim.

data_elements.name: Decomposition basis
data_elements.description: Coded value stating whether a recorded decomposition is lexical (form-level) or an asserted semantic composition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Coordination mode, component references and decomposition basis are qualifiers of the concept record itself. There is no standard-defined document for pre-coordination, and inventing an artifact would present unsupported structure as canonical when the primary source states that no such pattern has been established.

findings.name: Compound one-to-many equivalence across vocabularies
findings.description: ISO 25964-2 recognises that equivalence between vocabularies is often not one to one and provides compound equivalence, where a concept in one vocabulary is expressed by combining several concepts in another. The iso-thes vocabulary carries this as CompoundEquivalence with plusUF and plusUse, plus SplitNonPreferredTerm for a concept that is not directly present but is representable by combining preferred terms. SKOS has no native construct for this: a consumer reading plain SKOS will see either nothing or a set of unqualified matches, so the combination operator and the degradation behaviour must both be recorded.

questions.text: Which set of target concepts jointly expresses this concept, and in which vocabulary do they sit?
answer_data: Ordered or unordered set of target concept references forming the equivalence
Reference to the target vocabulary and its bound release
Direction of the equivalence, from this concept to the set

questions.text: Which combination operator applies to the target set, and which construct carries it when the interchange format has no compound-equivalence class?
answer_data: Combination operator: conjunctive or disjunctive
Construct or extension used to carry the operator

answer_data: Degradation rule, such as suppression or emission as separate close matches

bundles.name: Cross-scheme mapping, alignment and interchange
bundles.description: How a concept is connected to concepts in other schemes, aligned to formal ontology terms, and moved between systems and serializations without losing or over-stating meaning.
bundles.rationale: SKOS separates mapping properties from within-scheme semantic relations only by convention, and defines exactMatch as transitive and symmetric while closeMatch is symmetric but not transitive; broadMatch and narrowMatch are simultaneously sub-properties of broader and narrower, so cross-scheme assertions leak into the hierarchical closure. Interoperability therefore needs explicit chain rules, alignment-entailment declarations and format-neutral projection rules rather than being treated as an export detail.

layers.name: Cross-scheme mapping relations and mapping sets
layers.description: Mapping relation types and their formal properties, the packaging of mappings into sets or correspondences with cardinality and chain rules, and the caveats that apply when mapping across languages.

findings.name: Mapping relation types and their formal properties
findings.description: skos:mappingRelation is a sub-property of skos:semanticRelation. exactMatch is transitive and symmetric; closeMatch is symmetric but explicitly not transitive; broadMatch and narrowMatch are sub-properties of skos:broader and skos:narrower as well as of mappingRelation, so they participate in the hierarchical closure; relatedMatch is a sub-property of skos:related and is symmetric. Integrity condition S46 makes exactMatch disjoint with broadMatch and relatedMatch. Two facts are commonly missed: cross-scheme use of the mapping properties is a convention, not a formal requirement, and SKOS supplies no integrity condition making a same-scheme mapping inconsistent.

findings.name: Mapping sets, cardinality, binding and chain limits
findings.description: Mappings are managed as sets rather than as isolated statements. XKOS provides Correspondence, which compares two schemes, and ConceptAssociation with sourceConcept and targetConcept, allowing many-to-many associations to be reified and described. ISO 25964-2 similarly organises equivalence, hierarchical and associative mappings between vocabularies. Chain composition must be conservative: exactMatch is transitive so exact chains compose, but closeMatch is not transitive and a chain mixing types must not be composed at all. Every set binds to specific releases of the two schemes it compares; the releases themselves are issued by the lifecycle area.

findings.name: Multilingual and cross-lingual mapping caveats
findings.description: A concept is a language-independent node: SKOS attaches labels in many languages to one concept and permits only one preferred label per language tag, so a translation is normally a label of the same concept rather than a mapping to a different concept. Where two vocabularies are maintained in different languages, ISO 25964 treats cross-lingual equivalence as graded - exact, inexact, partial, one-to-many or absent. BCP 47 tags identify the language, script and region of a string; matching tags on two labels says nothing about whether the labels denote the same concept, and equal tags must never be used as evidence of equivalence.

layers.name: Formal alignment and interchange
layers.description: Connecting the concept to formal ontology terms with an explicit statement of entailment, and moving the concept's relation and mapping structure between systems and serializations with declared closure, crosswalks and losses.

findings.name: Semantic alignment to ontology classes, properties and individuals
findings.description: Aligning a concept to an ontology term is not the same as mapping it to another concept. OWL 2 gives owl:equivalentClass a set-extensional meaning over individuals, rdfs:subClassOf transitive and reflexive subsumption, and owl:sameAs identity of individuals, and each licenses a reasoner to draw consequences the vocabulary editor may not intend. OntoLex sits deliberately between the two worlds: LexicalConcept is a subclass of skos:Concept and is connected to entries by evokes and lexicalizedSense, while denotes and reference point at ontology predicates. DCAT shows the practical consequence, allowing a taxonomy to be a concept scheme, a collection or an ontology. The alignment predicate and its entailment scope must therefore be recorded with the alignment, not assumed.

findings.name: Import, export, projection and crosswalk behaviour
findings.description: RDF 1.1 establishes that the abstract structure of identifiers, values and statements is independent of any concrete serialization, and that identifiers have global scope, so JSON, YAML, Markdown, tabular files, Turtle and JSON-LD are projections of one assertion set. Interchange therefore turns on three decisions that must be declared rather than implied: which closure is included (concept alone, direct relations, whole scheme, or transitive neighbourhood); how references that leave the closure are represented so they are not read as missing data; and which constructs are lossy in the target model - refined hierarchical kinds, compound equivalence and reified associations are the usual casualties. Namespace and identifier resolution follow the published-vocabulary recipes: term identifiers stay stable while version information moves into the served document.

owner_package_requirements: Name one maintenance agency for every concept scheme the Dimension hosts, and record whether that agency or the Dimension issues authoritative concept identifiers, before any membership, relation or mapping assertion is accepted.
Register the namespace in which the Dimension mints concept identifiers, and never re-mint an identifier for a concept governed by an external scheme; reference the external identifier instead.
Declare, per scheme pair, whether cross-scheme mappings are authored locally or imported from an external correspondence publisher, and which of the two prevails on conflict.

Declare which relation kinds the Dimension supports - refined hierarchy, refined association, compound equivalence, reified many-to-many mapping - and the degradation applied to unsupported kinds on import and export.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Concept identifiers are dereferenceable IRIs in a namespace the publisher controls, designed as hash or slash namespaces following the W3C publishing recipes. Term identifiers stay stable across releases while version information is carried in the served document, and no label, language tag, notation or date is encoded in the identifier.

Parent registry record WM-KNW-002 for the concept-scheme model that governs scheme identity and release policy.
IANA Language Subtag Registry for BCP 47 subtags used to scope cross-lingual assertions.
Namespace registrations for aligned vocabularies: SKOS, SKOS-XL, iso-thes and XKOS.

canonicalization_rules: Relation, mapping, membership and alignment assertions canonicalise to an unordered set of subject-predicate-object statements over identifiers; serialization choice, statement order, prefix binding and file layout carry no meaning.
Only the direct form of a hierarchical relation is canonical; transitive forms and inverse statements are derived views and are excluded from the canonical set even when materialised.
Language-tagged values canonicalise to BCP 47 case conventions, and legacy or non-BCP-47 codes are normalised before any comparison.
Mapping sets canonicalise with their two compared schemes and bound releases in the header, so the same assertions bound to different releases are distinct sets.
patch_rules: A patch adds or withdraws individual assertions and identifies each by both endpoints plus the relation or mapping type; a whole-set replacement is never implied.
Absence of an assertion in a patch is never a withdrawal; withdrawal requires an explicit removal instruction.

A patch that would create an integrity violation - an associative link across an existing hierarchical path, or an exact match alongside a broad or related match for the same pair - is rejected as a unit rather than partially applied.
Patches never edit derived structure; changing a direct assertion marks the affected closure stale for recomputation.
compatibility_rules: Adding a refined relation kind alongside an existing plain hierarchical assertion is backward compatible; replacing the plain assertion with a refined-only one is breaking for consumers that read plain SKOS.

Strengthening a mapping from close match to exact match is breaking for consumers that compose chains, because exact match is transitive and close match is not; it must be released as a breaking change.
Withdrawing a scheme membership or a top-concept declaration is breaking for navigation entry points and must be announced with a replacement entry point.
Adding a new mapping set is compatible; re-binding an existing set to different scheme releases is breaking and requires a new series entry.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the maintenance agency of the governing concept scheme, or by the publisher of a correspondence, as published by that authority.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in a namespace the publisher controls and can dereference, following the published-vocabulary recipes.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only where no authoritative or governed identifier exists and always recorded as locally minted.
A label, notation string, language tag, filename or date is never used as an identifier; such values may only qualify an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All recorded times use RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Where they differ, the event time at which a relation, mapping or withdrawal was asserted is recorded separately from the observation or ingestion time at which this model received or imported it, and values normalise to UTC before ordering or comparison.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Mapping sets and interchange packages that are issued repeatedly carry a monotonically increasing series number together with the identifiers of the two bound scheme releases. The series number and release identifiers form part of the artifact name and never part of a concept identifier, and a withdrawn series number is not reused.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every exported artifact carries a content digest over its canonical assertion set plus the assertion count. An import whose digest or count does not reproduce is quarantined rather than merged; out-of-closure references are reported in the manifest rather than silently dropped, and constructs lost in translation are named in an explicit loss declaration.

policies: Within-scheme semantic relations and cross-scheme mapping relations are recorded as distinct assertion kinds and are never collapsed into a single undifferentiated link, even where the underlying standard permits both to appear between the same pair.

Every inferred structure - transitive closure, symmetric inverse, composed mapping chain, entailed alignment consequence - is marked as derived, is never written back as an authored assertion, and is invalidated when a contributing assertion changes.

No conformance to an external standard is claimed. External standards are recorded as alignments with a verifiable reference, and known conflicts between them are recorded rather than resolved by silent preference.

Conservative reading of relation semantics is the default: where a source declares a property non-transitive, asymmetric or disjoint, the model does not licence the stronger reading even where a consumer would find it convenient.

read: Resolve a concept's asserted relations, mappings, alignments, scheme memberships and grouping memberships by identifier, with each result marked authored or derived.
Traverse from a scheme's declared or computed entry points to a bounded depth, returning grouping nodes typed distinctly from concepts.
Retrieve mapping assertions filtered by target scheme, mapping type, containing set and bound release, together with the chain-composition rules that apply.
create: Create a relation or mapping only when both endpoints resolve, the endpoint types are legal for the construct, and the relation kind is supported by the governing scheme.
Register a mapping set with its two compared schemes and their bound releases before any member association is added to it.
Reject at creation any assertion that would violate a declared integrity condition, and record the rejection reason for the submitter.
update: Change a relation kind or mapping type by explicit re-assertion carrying the prior value, so consumers can detect a strengthening or weakening rather than inferring it from a diff.
Re-bind a mapping set to a different scheme release as an explicit, announced operation; bindings never drift implicitly when a referenced scheme is re-released.
Derived closures and inverse statements are recomputed rather than edited; an attempt to update a derived statement is rejected.
delete: Withdrawing a relation, mapping, membership or alignment records an explicit tombstone that keeps both endpoint identifiers, the withdrawn relation or mapping type, the withdrawal event time and the observation time, so downstream caches can retract rather than silently diverge.
Concept and mapping-set identifiers are not reused after withdrawal, and a withdrawn series number is retired; a tombstone is itself never deleted by this model.

Retention periods, physical erasure, legal disposition and any obligation to destroy records are outside this model's boundary: the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the governance and lifecycle area of WM-KNW-006 own execution, and this model only exposes the tombstone and the references those owners need to act on.

roles.name: Scheme maintenance agency
responsibilities: Owns the authoritative concept identifiers and the within-scheme relation set
Decides whether polyhierarchy, refined relation kinds and pre-coordinated compounds are permitted
Declares the scheme's top concepts, or the entry-point rule when none are declared

roles.name: Relation editor
responsibilities: Asserts and withdraws direct hierarchical and associative relations inside a scheme
Applies and records the justification test before a hierarchical assertion is created
Resolves reported disjointness violations between associative and hierarchical assertions

roles.name: Mapping curator
responsibilities: Authors, reviews and withdraws cross-scheme mappings and compound equivalences
Chooses the mapping type and records what is deliberately not being claimed
Maintains mapping sets, their bound scheme releases and their chain-composition rules

roles.name: Interoperability engineer
responsibilities: Maintains crosswalk specifications and their tested directions
Defines export closure rules, out-of-closure reference handling and loss declarations
Runs round-trip tests and publishes the list of lossy constructs per target model

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Respects the authored-versus-derived marking and never persists derived structure as authored
Honours the declared chain-composition and traversal limits
Reads the loss declaration and out-of-closure manifest before treating an import as complete

access.default_rule: Relation, mapping, membership, grouping and alignment assertions are readable by any agent permitted to read the concept itself. Write access is restricted to the role that owns the relevant scheme or mapping set, as declared by the adopting Dimension.
exceptions: Draft or unreviewed mappings are withheld from public export until released by the mapping curator.
Mappings to a third-party scheme whose licence forbids redistribution are readable internally but excluded from export packages.
Deprecated or hidden relations are exposed only to editing roles, and tombstones are exposed to consumers that need retraction signals.
Where an adopting Dimension applies a stricter policy, that policy prevails and the difference is recorded rather than overridden here.
audit_requirements: Each assertion and withdrawal carries who asserted it and both an event time and an observation time under the timestamp rule; persistence, retention, integrity protection and inspection of the resulting audit trail are executed by the governance area and the adopting Dimension, not by this model.
Export and import operations record the closure rule, crosswalk and loss declaration applied, so a receiving party can reconstruct what was and was not transmitted.

read_order: AGENTS.md as the entry point, regardless of whether records are held in a document store, a graph store, a database or a repository
Specification URL: scope, boundaries, relation and mapping semantics, and what must not be inferred
Storage type URL: how assertions, tombstones and mapping sets are persisted in this deployment
Interface URL: how identifiers are resolved and how relations, mappings and closures are retrieved
Processes URL: assertion, mapping, validation, import and export procedures and the roles that own them

coverage.claim: This pass covers the relationship, scheme and interoperability surface of WM-KNW-006 Concept / Term, grounded primarily in the W3C SKOS Recommendation and its SKOS-XL extension, the ISO 25964 model and its iso-thes RDF expression, XKOS, OntoLex-Lemon, OWL 2, RDF 1.1, BCP 47 and DCAT. It deliberately distinguishes within-scheme semantic relations from cross-scheme mapping relations, treats transitivity, symmetry, disjointness and mapping chains conservatively, and leaves lexical content, lifecycle, governance, provenance, access and quality to their owning areas. It is not a complete model of the concept, and no conformance to any cited standard is claimed.

checklist.notes: Identity priority names the maintenance agency's authoritative identifier first, then a governed dereferenceable IRI in a controlled namespace, then a locally minted UUID or ULID. Labels, notations, language tags, filenames and dates are explicitly barred as identifiers. Concept identity is asserted to be language independent and unaffected by mappings or grouping membership.

Concept, term and scheme lifecycle, versioning, deprecation and succession are owned by the lifecycle area of WM-KNW-006. This pass carries scheme release identifiers only as binding parameters of a mapping set and records iso-thes status as a referenced value; it defines no state machine and issues no releases.

Direct hierarchical assertion versus derived closure, refined generic/partitive/instantial kinds, associative relations with symmetry and disjointness, grouping constructs, compound composition and cross-scheme mappings are each modelled separately with their governing source and formal properties cited.

Covered only for the surface this pass owns: RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset, event time separated from observation or ingestion time, and mapping sets bound to specific scheme releases so that time-dependent correspondences are explicit. XKOS temporal and sequential relation types are recorded as an association subtype. Validity periods of concepts themselves are lifecycle-owned.

Provenance records, attribution and evidence packages are owned by the provenance area. This pass retains only what a relation needs to be interpretable - which scheme or mapping set an assertion belongs to, and a short strength or justification note held with the assertion - and imports carry supplied provenance references through without interpreting them.

Maintenance-agency authority, approval workflow and change control are governance-owned. This pass records which scheme or mapping set owns an assertion, so that write scope can be resolved, but grants no authority and defines no approval process.

SKOS integrity conditions on collection and scheme disjointness, associative/hierarchical disjointness and mapping-type disjointness are evaluated, along with cycle detection, closure staleness and round-trip loss testing. The integrity function reports findings only; enforcement gating and exception approval belong to the governance area.

A default read/write rule, scopes and exceptions are declared for schema completeness and to mark boundaries such as licence-restricted third-party mappings. Permission evaluation, enforcement and audit persistence are executed by the governance area and the adopting Dimension; the merge takes canonical service layers from governance.

Withdrawal semantics are defined for this model's own records: explicit tombstones retaining both endpoints, the withdrawn type and both timestamps, with no identifier reuse. Retention periods, physical erasure and legal disposition are explicitly assigned to the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the governance and lifecycle area, which own execution.

Cross-scheme mapping types with their formal properties, mapping sets with cardinality and release binding, conservative chain composition, alignment to ontology terms with declared entailment scope, crosswalk specifications, closure rules, out-of-closure reference handling and lossy-construct declarations are all modelled, with format neutrality grounded in the RDF abstract syntax.

The zero-scheme, single-scheme and multi-scheme cases are all modelled, membership is required to be asserted rather than derived from relations, and top concepts are treated as declared entry points rather than derived roots.

Transitivity, symmetry and disjointness are taken directly from the SKOS Reference, including the awkward consequence that broad and narrow matches are simultaneously hierarchical properties and the fact that same-scheme mapping is not formally inconsistent.

Language independence of the concept node, graded cross-lingual equivalence, BCP 47 subtag scoping with canonicalisation, and the explicit rule that matching language tags are not evidence of semantic equivalence.

Modelled from ISO 25964-2 compound equivalence, the iso-thes CompoundEquivalence and SplitNonPreferredTerm constructs and the OntoLex decomp module, but the SKOS Primer states that established patterns for pre-coordination have not emerged in the SKOS community. There is therefore no standard-native construct, and the local structure is marked provisional rather than canonical.
Alignment target kind, predicate and declared entailment scope are modelled from OWL 2 and OntoLex, with the reasoning environment referenced rather than owned.

known_omissions: The clause-level normative text of ISO 25964-1 and ISO 25964-2 and of ANSI/NISO Z39.19 was not read; those standards are behind paywalls or downloads that could not be retrieved, so their content is taken from the standards bodies' own published descriptions and from the iso-thes RDF expression. Specific clause numbers are deliberately not cited.
The ISO 1087:2019 catalogue page blocks automated retrieval, so no ISO 1087 clause text was read; it corroborates the generic/partitive distinction only, and no structural node rests on it alone.

SSSOM (Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings) and comparable mapping-exchange formats used in life sciences were not researched, so the mapping-set artifact is not aligned to them; adopters in those domains should treat that as an open alignment.

Confidence, similarity scoring and probabilistic mapping justification are not modelled; only a free-text strength basis is carried, which is weaker than what several mapping-exchange formats support.
Faceted classification and citation-order rules beyond node labels and facet indicators are not modelled.
The ISO 25964 XML exchange schema is referenced only through the crosswalk finding; its element-level structure was not enumerated.
No treatment of concept collections as query-time facets, or of collection-driven display ordering beyond the ordered member position.
conflicts: SKOS declares broadMatch and narrowMatch as sub-properties of both skos:broader/skos:narrower and skos:mappingRelation, so a cross-scheme mapping also enters the within-scheme transitive hierarchical closure. This cuts against the clean separation of semantic and mapping relations that the SKOS Primer presents, and the model records the leak explicitly rather than resolving it.

The SKOS Reference states that restricting mapping properties to different schemes is a convention and supplies no integrity condition against same-scheme mapping, while common practice and the Primer treat cross-scheme use as the rule. The model records the convention and permits the local rule to be stricter.

SKOS defines no integrity condition preventing a declared top concept from also asserting a broader concept in the same scheme, whereas thesaurus practice generally treats top terms as roots. The model treats top concepts as declared entry points and flags the coexistence rather than rejecting it.

ISO 25964 supports compound equivalence and split non-preferred terms, and XKOS supports reified many-to-many associations; SKOS has no native construct for either, so consumers reading plain SKOS lose the structure silently unless the loss is declared.

XKOS and iso-thes both refine broader, but with different property sets (specializes/isPartOf versus broaderGeneric/broaderPartitive/broaderInstantial); a scheme using one is not automatically interpretable by a consumer expecting the other, and neither maps cleanly onto ISO 1087 terminology-science relation typing.

OntoLex-Lemon is a Community Group Report and explicitly not a W3C Standard, so its constructs carry lower normative weight than SKOS or OWL 2 even though they are the best available model for the lexical bridge and for decomposition.
regional_assumptions: Language identification is assumed to follow BCP 47. Vocabularies that use ISO 639-2/B codes, national locale codes or ad hoc language strings must be canonicalised before comparison, and the canonicalisation rule must be recorded.

Script and region subtags are assumed to be significant, not decorative: cases such as Simplified versus Traditional Chinese and Latin versus Cyrillic Serbian must not be collapsed when scoping a cross-lingual assertion.

ISO 25964 practice is strongest in European and library-sector thesauri; XKOS correspondence practice reflects statistical-agency and DDI usage. A deployment outside those sectors may find neither refinement set idiomatic.

No jurisdiction-specific legal constraint on mapping or on redistribution of third-party vocabularies is assumed beyond the general licence exception in the access rules; adopters must check the licence of every referenced scheme.
Right-to-left and bidirectional text handling in labels is a lexical-area concern and is not assumed to be solved by the language tag alone.
adversarial_checks: Checked whether SKOS forbids a declared top concept from also having a broader concept in the same scheme. It does not - the Reference states there is no such integrity condition - so top concepts are modelled as declared entry points, not as derived roots, and the coexistence is flagged rather than rejected.

Checked whether skos:broader is transitive before allowing any finding to store ancestor sets. It is not; only skos:broaderTransitive is. Closure is therefore modelled as a derived view that is never written back as an authored assertion.

Checked whether scheme membership propagates along semantic relations. The SKOS Reference explicitly denies the entailment and gives a counterexample, so membership must be asserted per concept and any derivation is marked as a local rule.

Checked whether exact-match chains and close-match chains may be composed together. closeMatch is explicitly not transitive, so heterogeneous and non-transitive chain composition is rejected by the chain function rather than merely discouraged.

Checked whether mapping properties are formally restricted to different concept schemes. They are restricted only by convention, and same-scheme mapping produces no inconsistency, so the model records this as an exception case caused typically by merging sources rather than asserting a prohibition the standard does not make.

Checked whether the OntoLex decomp module supports a claim that a compound concept is the semantic composition of its parts. It decomposes lexical entries, not concepts, so decomposition basis is recorded as lexical or semantic and a non-inference statement is required.

Checked whether an alignment to an ontology term may default to owl:sameAs or owl:equivalentClass. OWL 2 gives both strong extensional consequences and distinguishes individual identity from class equivalence, so the alignment predicate and its entailment scope must be declared and the weaker predicate is the default.

Checked every bundle, layer, finding and function against the composition ledger for target-owned semantics. Entailment execution was moved to the ontology-reasoning REFERENCE; lexical forms, senses and label relations to the OntoLex REFERENCE; scheme identity and release issuance to the WM-KNW-002 CHILD link; language subtag governance to the BCP 47 REFERENCE; and catalogue records to the DCAT REFERENCE. Lifecycle, governance, provenance, access enforcement, audit persistence, retention execution and quality measurement were removed to out_of_scope and boundary notes.

Checked that no artifact was declared where the content is purely a set of typed references; nine of thirteen findings are inline-only for that reason, and the three artifacts declared (mapping set, interchange package, crosswalk specification) each have independent identity, a publication series or a verifiable payload.
